questions.q: What is the Salesforce Lightning Design System (SLDS)?
options: A separate JavaScript framework that competes with LWC
A testing framework for LWC components
An Apex library for formatting currency and dates
Salesforce's design language and CSS framework -- the colors, spacing, typography, icons, and markup patterns that give Lightning Experience its consistent look
questions.explain: SLDS is Salesforce's design language and CSS framework. Base Lightning components already apply it internally, which is why they look consistent with the rest of the platform with no extra styling work.

questions.q: When an SLDS utility class is passed into a base component's `class` attribute, like `<lightning-button class="slds-m-around_medium">`, what happens to the component's own internal styling?
options: The internal SLDS classes are completely replaced by the new class
The component throws a runtime error because class cannot be set on base components
The utility class is added alongside the classes the component already renders internally -- it's additive, not a replacement
The button becomes unstyled entirely
questions.explain: Passing a class into a base component is additive -- the component keeps its own internal SLDS classes, and the added utility class rides alongside them for the specific adjustment you need.

questions.q: What naming change happened to SLDS class names starting in LWC API version 61.0?
options: Double-dash names (slds-p-around--small) switched to a single underscore (slds-p-around_small)
Underscore names (slds-p-around_small) switched to double-dash (slds-p-around--small)
All SLDS class names were renamed to use camelCase
SLDS utility classes were removed entirely in favor of inline styles
questions.explain: Starting in LWC API version 61.0, class names that previously used a double dash switched to a single underscore -- slds-p-around--small became slds-p-around_small.

questions.q: What determines whether a component should use the double-dash or underscore form of an SLDS class name?
options: The developer's personal preference, since both forms always work identically regardless of version
Whether the component uses @track or not
The component's apiVersion as set in its js-meta.xml file, relative to the 61.0 boundary
Whether the component is exposed to Lightning App Builder
questions.explain: The naming form depends on the component's targeted API version (set in js-meta.xml) relative to the 61.0 boundary where the change took effect -- not a stylistic choice independent of that version.

questions.q: What does this lesson recommend when no combination of SLDS utility classes achieves the exact styling result needed?
options: Override a base component's internal class names directly, such as .slds-input
Disable SLDS entirely for that component
Write your own CSS rule in the component's own .css file, applied through a custom class name you define
Switch the component from LWC to Aura
questions.explain: The correct fallback is custom CSS in the component's own stylesheet, applied via a class name you define yourself -- never by overriding a class name you don't own, which is the same rule from Lesson 24.
